Subject: Kubernetes on-prem acceptance criteria & hardware constraints

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the call today. To make sure our on-prem deployment runs smoothly we need a short, prescriptive acceptance checklist we can hand to our infra team and procurement. High level constraints / asks from our side: 

- Physical footprint: 2 racks at a single colo (no cross-rack compute for initial phase).
- Hardware inventory attached (site-inventory.csv) — 6 servers with 4xA100-class GPUs, 2x storage-only nodes.
- Security: We must use customer-managed KMS/HSM for any long-term model artifacts and keys, no private keys leaving the VPC.
- Network: Egress locked down; only approved monitoring endpoints and outbound to Redwood control-plane for updates (we can provide IP allowlist).
- Storage: Models and artifacts must be on encrypted blockstore; runtime KV/cache may use local NVMe but must never persist model artifacts.
- Tenancy: Separate node pools for inference (GPU), training/batch (GPU), and control/ops (CPU).
- Acceptance tests: cold-start latency for a 2048-token request under 150ms p50 on inference pool, 99.9% pod stability over 24h.

Can you confirm what you need from us (e.g., CSI driver version constraints, KMS attestation steps) and provide a short suggested node-packing and PV strategy we can use to approve the SOW?

Felix
IT Operations — Vanguard Healthcare

Hi Felix —

Thanks for the inventory and clear constraints. Quick technical proposal below (keeping to a minimal, auditable acceptance plan):

1) Node pools and packing
- inference-gpu-pool (3 nodes, each 4xGPU): dedicated for latency-sensitive replicas. Use kubelet eviction thresholds tuned for GPU allocation; ensure PodDisruptionBudgets across AZs (in your case, across racks).
- batch-gpu-pool (2 nodes, 4xGPU): lower-priority batch and offline ops with preemptible-style scheduling.
- control/ops-pool (2 nodes, CPU-only, 64GB RAM): control plane glue, logging/observability agents, CSI controller-hosts.
- storage-proxy (2 storage-only nodes): high-IO encrypted blockstore for model artifacts and backups.

Rationale: pack inference onto the 3 strongest hosts to keep NVMe locality for KV cache and avoid cross-node NVMe traffic. Keep storage-proxy nodes as the single attachment point for long-term blockstore.

2) PV strategy
- Long-term artifacts -> encrypted blockstore via CSI (we support AWS EBS-like workflow and on-prem iSCSI/NFS backed by blockstore). Require KMS integration (customer KMS) for CMKs; we’ll accept wrapped keys via HSM attestation.
- Runtime KV/cache -> local NVMe with ephemeral PodLocal cache (emptyDir with tmpfs for small caches & local NVMe for disk-backed KV). Ensure a node drain policy that flushes KV to a transient blob (no permanent model writes).
- Backups -> periodic snapshot to storage-proxy with server-side encryption managed by customer KMS.

3) CSI/KMS notes
- CSI driver: we recommend the in-tree CSI shim v3+ (we've validated with csi-block-1.2.0). If you run a different vendor, we need the exact driver binary to validate attach/detach semantics.
- KMS: we support KMIP and PKCS#11-backed HSMs. For attestation, provide an endpoint we can call during install; we need key-policy binding for the Redwood service account used by the backup controller.

4) Acceptance tests (suggested pass/fail items)
- PV attach/detach cycle test: attach model artifact volume to pod -> write/read checksum -> detach -> reattach on a different node.
- Cold-start latency benchmark: 100 requests, 2048 tokens, p50 <150ms, p95 <400ms (on inference pool).
- Failover: simulate node loss of 1 inference node; traffic should continue with <2x latency for in-flight connections and no data loss for ephemeral KV.
- CSI + KMS: create encrypted volume, write test file, verify KMS encryption metadata and that keys are customer-managed.

I’ve attached a concise BOM (nodegrid-bom.xlsx) with how we would allocate pods per host and approximate NVMe sizing. We’ll mark exact kernel/CIFS driver versions in the install playbook.

If this looks OK I’ll draft the install playbook and a 3-day validation runbook (hardware soak, PV cycle, perf test).

-Neha
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
